full_page.content:
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed carbon by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
1946, May 22
ST. FELIX FRIARY HUNTINGTON, IND. May 22nd 1946.
Miss Belle Lyke 26 W. Oneida St., Oswiego, New York
Dear Miss Lyke:
God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you well and that the, "kind of mixup" caused by my transfer hither, etc, may not be so grave as to be insurmount- able.
First I want to thank you for your constant zeal in the work of the poor foreign Missions as manifest from the realy laudable number of enrollments received from you these past years. However, while I have seen your name quite often, I have been force by circumstances to rely very much on others to keep up my correspondence and acknowledgements.
Notably ever since they took me in the ambulance to the Hospital where I remained for nine weeks, That was a couple of years back and for about sex months following I was able to do very little. I went to the Monastery- office; yes, but even after I was well on my feet again, there were so many callers that I had to give personal attention to, that/ I worked for 18 hours a day - as was sometimes the case - I could not attend to one quarter of my personal letters.
Since my transfer from St. Bonaventure's my personal callers have been by no means as heavy; though my letters - possibly because I have to take care of them myself - seem a heavy as ever; and you can imagine how I appreciate it to have someone like one of the Brothers or Fathers in Detroit continue their generous assistence in the work that, even with such help, often keeps me - with other duties - from 5 0'cl a.m. Il p.m.
